points.description: Seasonality: regular/periodic oscillations in the hydrologic data (e.g. monthly or seasonal events) repeating within a year, caused by the earth's rotation/revolution around the sun.
points.partial_credit: Half if only says it is regular/periodic or yearly, without cause or example.

points.description: Long-term oscillations: oscillations around the trend line/mean that occur over a very large (multi-year) period of time, as opposed to the short regular seasonal cycle.
points.partial_credit: Half if only says they happen over a long time without contrasting with seasonality or mentioning the mean/trend.

rubric.notes: Award full marks for each side if the central idea is stated in any wording: seasonality is regular, short (within-year) cycles tied to the earth's movement around the sun, while long-term oscillations occur over very long periods around the trend/mean. Give part marks for vague but relevant statements, such as only 'seasonal is yearly and long-term is longer'. Give no marks for unrelated or reversed descriptions. Extra wrong remarks don't cost marks unless they contradict the main idea.
